Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. Attached is our short security questionnaire focused on data residency, retention, and deletion for hosted APIs. High level asks:

1) Where do request payloads and model outputs live (region, physical boundaries) and for how long?
2) What is your default retention for request/response content, audit logs, and backups?
3) Can we request per-tenant immediate purge, and what proofs/certificates can you provide?
4) Do you offer region-locked storage for hosted customers (US-only / EU-only)?
5) Key management: do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for hosted?

We've attached the questionnaire (AuroraLens_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf). Our procurement/security team (cc'd) would like a written response for inclusion in our vendor review.

Hi Samira — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear asks. Below are concise answers mapped to your numbered items; I’ve attached a tailored retention matrix (retention-matrix-auroralens.xlsx) and links to our most recent SOC 2 attestation. If you want, Ben (cc) can set up a 30-minute call to walk through specifics.

1) Data residency:
- Hosted API requests and generated outputs are stored in the region you select at account provisioning (we support US and EU region options for hosted customers).
- Default physical boundaries are cloud-region-level (major cloud provider regions). For customers requiring stricter controls we offer Dedicated and Private deployments.

2) Default retention (hosted API):
- Request + response content (full payloads): 30 days by default for troubleshooting, billing, and quality monitoring purposes. Customers may opt-in to extended retention for analytics (90 / 365 days) via contractual addendum.
- KV/prefix caches and model inference caches: ephemeral by design; default TTL is 24 hours and no persistent copies are kept beyond the configured TTL.
- Audit/system logs (operational metadata, not PII): retained 365 days by default for security monitoring and compliance.
- Backups/snapshots (cold store): encrypted backups kept up to 90 days by default; backups are rotated and encrypted and accessible only to engineering operations under strict change control.

3) Per-tenant purge / proof of deletion:
- We support on-demand tenant data expunge requests. Process: submit a support ticket referencing the tenant ID + deletion scope. Hot storage purge: removed from live stores within 48 hours; cache eviction immediate. Full expunge from backups: completed within 90 days (we validate backup retention windows to maintain safe restore capability).
- Evidence/certificate: we can issue a deletion certificate (PDF) tied to the support ticket and provide a timestamped audit log excerpt showing the purge operation. See attached example (data-deletion-cert-auroralens.pdf).

4) Region-locking and geo controls:
- Hosted customers can select a primary region (US or EU) at onboarding. Data is constrained to that region for processing and storage at rest. Cross-region failover is available as an opt-in with documented rules; default behavior does not replicate tenant payloads outside the selected region.

5) Key management (KMS/HSM):
- We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for encryption-at-rest in hosted tier (major cloud KMS providers). For customers requiring HSM-backed keys or isolated key material, we recommend Dedicated/Private deployments where we can enable HSM integrations.

Additional notes:
- De-identification: customers can request that training/quality pipelines exclude stored payloads; by default stored payloads are used only for billing and diagnostics unless you opt-in for quality improvements.
- Evidence & attestations: SOC 2 report and our data handling playbook are available via the customer portal. Link: https://portal.redwood.ai/soc2-report/latest

If you’d like a written summary tailored to specific AuroraLens policies (or a contract clause), Ben and I can draft an addendum.

Hi Samira — quick clarifications inline below.

> For the deletion certificate, can you provide an SLA for the hot purge (is 48 hours a contractual SLA or an operational target)?
- Operational target: 48 hours for hot storage purge is our operational target for hosted customers and is included as an objective in our standard DPA. We can convert that to a contractual SLA for enterprise customers on Dedicated or with an addendum for critical tenants. Ben can follow up on contractual language that meets AuroraLens’ procurement needs.

> Can you confirm whether encrypted backups are also subject to the same region-locking guarantees? We need to ensure cold backups for AuroraLens remain US-only.
- Yes: backups for region-locked hosted tenants are stored in the same region by default. For additional assurance we can provide a backup storage manifest and periodic attestation of snapshot locations. If you need stricter guarantees (e.g., legal hold, immutable snapshots in a single region) we recommend Dedicated/Private where we can enforce placement controls at a platform level.

> Is bring-your-own-key available during initial onboarding or only after you convert an account?
- BYOK is available during onboarding for hosted customers (subject to KMS provider compatibility). We’ll coordinate key setup during account provisioning — there’s no need to convert later unless you want HSM-backed keys which require Dedicated/Private.

Next steps:
- I’ll post the deletion certificate sample to the Drive link and open a dedicated support ticket to capture the tenant ID / scope.
- Ben will reach out to schedule a 30-minute call to go over contractual language and any Dedicated/Private options if you prefer those.

Links/attachments provided: data-deletion-cert-auroralens.pdf (attached), retention matrix (Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/secure/auroralens/retention-matrix). SOC 2 attestation: https://portal.redwood.ai/soc2-report/latest
